source.title: Multi-Level Firing with Spiking DS-ResNet: Enabling Better and Deeper Directly-Trained Spiking Neural Networks
source.authors: Lang Feng; Qianhui Liu; Huajin Tang; De Ma; Gang Pan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure labels and plotted curves are garbled, so the figure-only values cannot be read precisely.
record.tranche_reason: Tests depth-related training degradation in directly trained spiking networks on CIFAR-10, extending the claim to SNNs and to modified residual architectures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-accuracy curves and explicit textual comparisons for depth and architecture. Cited results from other papers and standalone classification-accuracy results are not catalog rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual architectures, normalization and He initialization to develop directly trained spiking networks. Its depth experiments compare spiking residual networks with different firing and shortcut arrangements, rather than the plain batch-normalized networks and identity-shortcut counterparts specified by V3. These results establish a related SNN finding, but do not test the stated versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: MLF improves gradient propagation and neuronal expression, while DS-ResNet improves discrete-spike identity mapping and suppresses dormant units. They report alleviated degradation and successful scaling to 68-layer SNNs. The explicit training-accuracy depth comparison is 14 versus 32 layers; the additional depths are summarized using test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Directly trains spiking neural networks using STBP, MLF, and spiking DS-ResNet; the depth comparison is on CIFAR10 and includes tdBN.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and architecture (MLF and spiking DS-ResNet) change the reported degradation outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, 32-layer ResNet-SNN has lower training accuracy than its 14-layer counterpart. MLF alleviates this degradation, and DS-ResNet with MLF further resolves it according to the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directly trained spiking residual networks can exhibit depth-related training degradation; multi-level firing and shortcut arrangements that preserve discrete spikes can alleviate it.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix G reports non-convergence for spiking VGG16 without MLF and training crashes in four of five 32-layer ResNet-SNN runs. MLF or DS-ResNet prevents the reported crashes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Surrogate-gradient spiking networks can fail through catastrophic gradient vanishing, with stability depending on firing and residual-block design.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 reports faster training-loss convergence with MLF; Table F.1 reports average weight-gradient increases of 42.2% and 46.1% for two and three firing levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Expanding surrogate-gradient coverage through multi-level firing improves gradient propagation and convergence in directly trained spiking networks.

record.problems: Training-accuracy values in Figure 5 are not stated in text and the plotted curves are not legible in the supplied text. The paper reports five-run averages for several classification-accuracy results, but does not report uncertainty for the training-accuracy comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible training-accuracy results were omitted. Table 1 and Tables 2–3 report classification accuracy, not training error or depth-related training accuracy; Figure 4 reports dormant-unit proportions and loss rather than the version's depth-related training-accuracy measure.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in the specified convolutional networks, including random-label training and model-size or regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized networks versus identity-shortcut counterparts, longer-training controls, and the tanh-initialization and Fixup results.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth; initialization is held fixed.
Training relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Normalization versus no-normalization comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: States are assessed against the supplied claim versions. The textual SNN findings remain interpretable despite unreadable curve values, but do not warrant verdicts on V3. Appendix G's failures do not test initialization or learning-rate stability claims because neither initialization nor a stability threshold is compared.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report whether training classification error reaches zero or near zero, or test corrupted or random labels, model size, or early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or neuron-width sweep.
Does not test ImageNet or plain batch-normalized ANN networks. The tested SNNs use tdBN and spiking activations; the degradation comparison varies MLF and DS-ResNet as well as depth.
Uses He et al. initialization but does not compare initializations or test the initialization claims.
Does not test learning rates above a stability limit, loss curvature, or sharpness.
Uses tdBN in its SNN architectures but does not compare batch normalization with no normalization or test the stated speed and learning-rate effects.

rows.subject: ResNet-SNN without MLF, 14-layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 without MLF; training accuracy compared across depths.
rows.measure: Training accuracy over training; plotted curve only.
rows.note: The text identifies this as the shallower comparison but does not state its training-accuracy value.
rows.check: A shallower spiking residual comparator, not a plain batch-normalized network testing V3; its individual training accuracy is unreadable.

rows.subject: ResNet-SNN without MLF, 32-layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 without MLF; compared with the 14-layer network.
rows.measure: Training accuracy over training; text says deeper model has lower training accuracy than the 14-layer model.
rows.baseline: 14-layer ResNet-SNN without MLF; exact value not stated
rows.note: The authors explicitly describe serious degradation at 32 layers and lower training accuracy than the shallower model.
rows.check: Lower training accuracy at 32 versus 14 layers is explicitly reported, but for spiking residual networks whose shortcuts do not implement identity mapping effectively. This does not establish a reversal of V3.

rows.subject: ResNet-SNN with MLF, 14-layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with MLF; training accuracy compared across depths.
rows.measure: Training accuracy over training; plotted curve only.
rows.note: The text says MLF improves training accuracy but does not give a numeric training-accuracy value.
rows.check: A spiking residual comparator using multi-level firing, outside V3's specified comparison; its individual training accuracy is unreadable.

rows.subject: ResNet-SNN with MLF, 32-layer

rows.measure: Training accuracy over training; text says degradation is alleviated.
rows.baseline: ResNet-SNN without MLF; exact value not stated
rows.note: The authors describe degradation as alleviated, not fully solved, after adding MLF.
rows.check: The text establishes alleviation of SNN degradation with MLF, but this firing-method intervention does not measure V3's plain-network versus identity-shortcut effect.

rows.note: The text identifies this architecture as the final comparison but does not state the shallower model's training-accuracy value.
rows.check: A comparator for the proposed spiking architecture, not the plain network named by V3; its individual training accuracy is unreadable.

rows.subject: Spiking DS-ResNet with MLF, 32-layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with spiking DS-ResNet and MLF; compared with shallower depth.
rows.measure: Training accuracy over training; text says degradation is further solved.
rows.baseline: Spiking DS-ResNet with MLF at 14 layers; exact value not stated
rows.note: The authors say the degradation problem is further solved with spiking DS-ResNet and MLF; the plotted values are not legible.
rows.check: The authors report further resolution of SNN degradation using DS-ResNet plus MLF. This combined architecture and firing intervention does not isolate the identity-shortcut comparison specified by V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
